description: A tour of our Solar System written for 8–12 year olds by Wikijunior volunteers: the Sun, each planet and its main moons, the asteroid and Kuiper belts, comets, and the story of space travel. Each day you read one short page together online, then narrate, sketch, or add to a planet notebook. It's a free, openly licensed children's book; every page is free to read on Wikibooks.
includes: Link to the free Wikibooks page for every lesson
A planet notebook page for each world: size, day, year, and namesake
Simple hands-on extras: scale models, weight math, night-sky watching
Questions with answers for every lesson

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Studying the Solar System
steps: Read the introduction together
Talk about the difference between an astronomer and an astrophysicist
Start a Solar System notebook with a title page
questions: What do we call scientists who study space?

lessons.title: Lesson 2: What Is in the Solar System?
steps: Read the first half, through 'What holds it together?'
Draw the Sun with the inner planets, the asteroid belt and the outer planets in order
Narrate why the planets keep going around the Sun
questions: Which four planets are the inner planets?
What force keeps the planets orbiting the Sun?

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Who Discovered the Solar System?
steps: Read the second half, from 'Who discovered the Solar System?'
Make a mini timeline: Aristarchus, Copernicus, Galileo
Narrate how the Solar System formed from a cloud of dust and gas
questions: Which new invention did Galileo point at the sky?
Which galaxy is our Solar System part of?

lessons.title: Lesson 4: The Sun
steps: Read the page together
Draw the Sun's layers: core, radiative zone, photosphere, corona
Never look straight at the Sun; talk about why
questions: What two gases is the Sun mostly made of?
About how often does the sunspot cycle repeat?
What lights in the sky near the North Pole can solar flares cause?

lessons.title: Lesson 5: Mercury
steps: Read the page together
Make a notebook page: size, day, year, namesake
Narrate: tell back three things you learned
questions: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
How long is a year on Mercury?
Who was the Roman god Mercury?

lessons.title: Lesson 6: Venus
steps: Read the page together
Add Venus to your notebook
Compare Venus and Earth in a two-column chart
questions: Why is Venus called Earth's twin?
Is a day on Venus longer or shorter than its year?
What is the tall mountain on Venus called?
answers: It is nearly the same size as Earth

lessons.title: Lesson 7: Earth
steps: Read the page together
On a globe, find all seven continents and five oceans
Narrate what moving plates can cause
questions: Which planet from the Sun is Earth?
Why does Earth have seasons?
Why do we have a leap year about every four years?
answers: To use up the extra quarter day each year

lessons.title: Lesson 8: The Moon
steps: Read the page together
Look at the Moon tonight (or a photo) and find the dark maria
Sketch the Moon in your notebook
questions: What are the dark areas on the Moon called?
Why do we always see the same side of the Moon?
answers: It spins once in the same time it takes to orbit Earth (about 27 days)

lessons.title: Lesson 9: Mars
steps: Read the page together
Add Mars to your notebook
Compare Olympus Mons with Mount Everest using a quick drawing
questions: Why is Mars red?
What is the highest mountain in the Solar System?
How long is a year on Mars?

lessons.title: Lesson 10: Phobos and Deimos
steps: Read both moon pages
Shape two lumpy 'potato moons' from clay or playdough
Narrate how the two moons are alike and different
questions: Which moon of Mars is bigger, Phobos or Deimos?
What will Mars' gravity probably do to Phobos one day?

lessons.title: Lesson 11: The Asteroid Belt
steps: Read the page together
Mark the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter on your Solar System drawing
Narrate: tell back three things you learned
questions: Between which two planets is the asteroid belt?
What is the biggest object in the asteroid belt?

units.title: Unit 3: Jupiter, Saturn and Their Moons

lessons.title: Lesson 12: Jupiter
steps: Read the page together
Add Jupiter to your notebook
Draw the Great Red Spot and compare it with Earth's size
questions: What is the largest planet in the Solar System?
About how long is a day on Jupiter?
Who was Jupiter in Roman stories?
answers: The king of the Roman gods

lessons.title: Lesson 13: Amalthea and Io
steps: Read both moon pages
Paint or color Io's yellow and orange volcanic surface
Narrate: tell back three things you learned
questions: Which object is the reddest in the Solar System?
What makes Io so full of volcanoes?
answers: Jupiter's pull causes tides inside it

lessons.title: Lesson 14: Europa
steps: Read the page together
Imagine and draw a creature that might live in an ocean under ice
Narrate why scientists are so curious about Europa
questions: What might lie under Europa's icy surface?

lessons.title: Lesson 15: Ganymede and Callisto
steps: Read both moon pages
Make a chart of the four Galilean moons: Io, Europa, Ganymede, Callisto
Narrate: tell back three things you learned
questions: What is the largest moon in the Solar System?
What are the only features on Callisto's surface?

lessons.title: Lesson 16: Saturn
steps: Read the page together
Add Saturn and its rings to your notebook
Test which things float in a bowl of water and talk about why Saturn could float
questions: What are Saturn's rings made of?
What do shepherd moons do?
Which day of the week is named after Saturn?
answers: Keep the ring particles in place with their gravity

lessons.title: Lesson 17: Titan
steps: Read the page together
Draw the Huygens probe parachuting down to Titan
Narrate: tell back three things you learned
questions: What makes Titan different from every other moon?
Which moon is the only one bigger than Titan?

lessons.title: Lesson 18: Mimas, Enceladus and Tethys
steps: Read the three short moon pages
Draw Mimas with its giant crater Herschel
Narrate one surprising fact about each moon
questions: What is the biggest crater on Mimas called?
What is the largest crater on Tethys called?

lessons.title: Lesson 19: Dione and Rhea
steps: Read both moon pages
Talk about what 'synchronous rotation' means using a ball and a lamp
Narrate: tell back three things you learned
questions: What are the bright wispy streaks on Dione?
Why does the same side of Rhea always face Saturn?
answers: It turns once in the same time it takes to orbit Saturn

lessons.title: Lesson 20: Hyperion, Iapetus and Phoebe
steps: Read the three moon pages
Color a two-tone Iapetus: one dark half, one bright half
Finish your chart of Saturn's moons
questions: Which moon of Saturn looks like a sponge?
Which way does Phoebe orbit compared with moons like Titan?

units.title: Unit 4: The Ice Giants and Beyond

lessons.title: Lesson 21: Uranus
steps: Read the page together
Add Uranus to your notebook
Roll a ball across the table to show a planet spinning on its side
questions: Who discovered Uranus?
How long is a year on Uranus?

lessons.title: Lesson 22: Miranda, Ariel and Umbriel
steps: Read the three moon pages
Note which spacecraft took the only close-up pictures
Narrate: tell back three things you learned
questions: Which spacecraft flew past Uranus in 1986?
Which is the darkest of Uranus' moons?

lessons.title: Lesson 23: Titania and Oberon
steps: Read both moon pages
Find the play The Tempest or A Midsummer Night's Dream and see the names that moons share
Narrate: tell back three things you learned
questions: What is the largest moon of Uranus?
Which moon of Uranus is the outermost of the major moons?

lessons.title: Lesson 24: Neptune
steps: Read the page together
Add Neptune to your notebook
Compare Neptune's winds with the fastest tornado on Earth
questions: What was the large dark storm Voyager saw on Neptune called?
Where are the fastest winds in the Solar System?

lessons.title: Lesson 25: Proteus, Triton and Nereid
steps: Read the three moon pages
Draw Triton's icy geysers
Narrate: tell back three things you learned
questions: What is the largest moon of Neptune?
What do scientists think Nereid might once have been?
answers: An asteroid captured by Neptune's gravity

lessons.title: Lesson 26: Pluto and Charon
steps: Read both pages
Add Pluto, the dwarf planet, to your notebook
Narrate why Pluto and Charon are sometimes called a double planet
questions: Who discovered Pluto, and in what year?
How long is a year on Pluto?

lessons.title: Lesson 27: Comets
steps: Read the page together
Make a comet: a ball of foil with streamers for a tail, and point the tail away from a lamp 'Sun'
Narrate: tell back three things you learned
questions: What is a good way to picture a comet?
What causes a meteor shower?
Who is a comet usually named after?
answers: Earth passing through dust left by a comet

lessons.title: Lesson 28: The Kuiper Belt and the Oort Cloud
steps: Read both pages
Add both regions to the edge of your Solar System drawing
Narrate: tell back three things you learned
questions: Where does the Kuiper belt lie?
What is the Oort cloud made of?

units.title: Unit 5: Exploring Space and Big Questions

lessons.title: Lesson 29: Space Exploration, Part 1
steps: Read from the beginning through 'The race to the Moon'
Make a timeline: Sputnik, Laika, Gagarin, Apollo 11
Narrate: tell back three things you learned
questions: What was the first satellite, and which country launched it?
Who was the first person in space?
Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
answers: Sputnik 1, launched by the Soviet Union

lessons.title: Lesson 30: Space Exploration, Part 2
steps: Read from 'The Space Shuttle' to the end
Draw your own idea for a spaceship of the future
Narrate: tell back three things you learned
questions: What big project did the Space Shuttle help to build?
Why can the Hubble Space Telescope see so clearly?

lessons.title: Lesson 31: Review: Puzzles and Test
steps: Try the puzzle page together
Answer the test questions out loud or on paper
Look back over your notebook and pick a favorite world
questions: Name the eight planets in order from the Sun.
answers: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune
lessons.notes: Look up any word you're unsure of in the book's Glossary page.

lessons.title: Lesson 32: Gravity, Mass and Weight
steps: Read the page together
Weigh a book on a kitchen scale and talk about whether its mass would change on the Moon
Narrate: tell back three things you learned

links.label: Read: About gravity, mass, and weight

questions: What is mass?
Would your mass change if you went to the Moon?
answers: The amount of material something is made of

lessons.title: Lesson 33: How the Solar System Was Born
steps: Read the page together
Blow up a dotted balloon to see how everything spreads apart as it grows
Narrate: tell back three things you learned

links.label: Read: How the Solar System was born

questions: About how long ago do scientists think the Big Bang happened?

lessons.title: Lesson 34: What Will Happen to the Solar System?
steps: Read the page together
Draw the Sun now and as a red giant
Narrate: tell back three things you learned

links.label: Read: What will happen to the Solar System in the future

questions: About how many more years will the Sun keep shining much as it does now?
What is the process called that makes the Sun's energy?

lessons.title: Lesson 35: Is There Life Out There?
steps: Read the page together
Talk about where in the Solar System life might be found, and why
Write or dictate your own guess, with a reason

links.label: Read: Is there life out there?

questions: What is the equation called that scientists use to guess how much life is out there?
About how many stars are in the Milky Way?
